insights.concise_text: The paper addresses Bottleneck B1, Bottleneck B2, and Bottleneck B3 by evaluating Formspring, Twitter, and Wikipedia datasets for personal attack, racism, and sexism without explicit feature engineering.

triple.subject: deep learning based models along with transfer learning
triple.object: Bottleneck B1, Bottleneck B2, and Bottleneck B3

insights.concise_text: Swear word list based filtering is unsuitable for cyberbullying detection because 78% of Formspring swearing posts are non-bullying and 82% of Twitter bullying posts use no swear words.

triple.subject: swear word list based filtering
triple.object: cyberbullying detection

insights.concise_text: Class imbalance in Formspring, Twitter, and Wikipedia datasets caused non-bullying bias, so oversampling bullying posts thrice significantly improved all DNN models.

triple.subject: oversampling bullying posts thrice
triple.object: all DNN models under class imbalance

insights.concise_text: Because Formspring has only 825 bullying instances, oversampling particularly helps the smallest dataset compared with Twitter and Wikipedia bullying classes of about 5K and 13K.

triple.subject: oversampling
triple.object: Formspring with 825 bullying instances

insights.concise_text: Task specific word embeddings capture SMP specific and topic specific cyberbullying style, and learned embeddings across multiple datasets show differences across cyberbullying topics and SMPs.

triple.subject: task specific word embeddings
triple.object: learned embeddings to show differences across cyberbullying topics and SMPs

insights.concise_text: Twitter dataset contains racism and sexism, and its learned embeddings consider word slave as similar to targets of racism and sexism.

triple.subject: Twitter dataset
triple.object: word slave to be similar to targets of racism and sexism

insights.concise_text: Wikipedia dataset contains personal attack, and its learned embeddings do not show the Twitter dataset bias for word slave toward targets of racism and sexism.

triple.subject: Wikipedia dataset
triple.object: word slave bias toward targets of racism and sexism

insights.concise_text: TL1 low recall and TL2 dramatic recall improvement jointly indicate that learned word embeddings, not direct model reuse, are essential for cross-dataset cyberbullying detection.

triple.subject: Feature Level Transfer Learning (TL2)
triple.object: Complete Transfer Learning (TL1) recall

insights.concise_text: TL3 transfers learned word embeddings and network weights but does not significantly improve over TL2, supporting that network weights are not essential for cyberbullying detection.

triple.subject: Model Level Transfer Learning (TL3)
triple.object: Feature Level Transfer Learning (TL2)

insights.concise_text: BLSTM with attention and feature level transfer learning achieves F1 scores of 0.94 for Wikipedia and Twitter, beating previous best F1 scores of 0.68 and 0.93.

triple.subject: BLSTM with attention and feature level transfer learning
triple.object: previous best F1 scores for Wikipedia and Twitter
